subject.title: [Bug] Session flush blocks write tool completely during compaction

question: Should silent memory-triggered compaction turns be allowed to write outside the configured daily memory file?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes a hard write boundary for a silent housekeeping run and cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Keep strict daily-memory-only writes
options.body: Preserve the current boundary and address user pain through scheduling, cancellation, or clearer recovery instead of allowing arbitrary workspace writes during flush.

options.title: Allow narrowly validated non-memory passthrough
options.body: Permit non-memory writes only through the normal workspace/sandbox guard with tests proving memory paths remain append-only and unsafe paths remain blocked.

options.title: Add an explicit opt-in escape hatch
options.body: Keep secure defaults and allow trusted operators to relax the guard through a documented, tested config or command path.

recommendation.title: Allow narrowly validated non-memory passthrough
recommendation.body: Permit non-memory writes only through the normal workspace/sandbox guard with tests proving memory paths remain append-only and unsafe paths remain blocked.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant history is the strict memory-flush guard and forwarding code that this decision would change.
